title: Acts Chapter 10 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Acts chapter 10 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Acts Chapter 10 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Acts Chapter 10.

questions.question: In Acts 10, which of the following appears FIRST in the chapter?
options: Peter went up upon the housetop to pray
Cornelius saw an angel of God in a vision
Peter saw a great sheet knit at the four corners
questions.correctAnswer: Cornelius was a centurion
questions.explanation: Acts 10:1 introduces Cornelius as a centurion before any other events mentioned.

questions.question: What was Cornelius's occupation?
questions.correctAnswer: A centurion
questions.explanation: Acts 10:1 states Cornelius was a centurion of the band called the Italian band.

questions.question: What kind of man was Cornelius described as?
options: A devout man who feared God
questions.correctAnswer: A devout man who feared God
questions.explanation: Acts 10:2 describes Cornelius as a devout man who feared God with all his house.

questions.question: Whom did Cornelius see in his vision?
questions.correctAnswer: An angel of God
questions.explanation: Acts 10:3 states Cornelius saw an angel of God coming to him in a vision.

questions.question: What did the angel of God say to Cornelius in the vision?
options: Cornelius, your prayers and alms are remembered by God
Peter is coming to see you
questions.correctAnswer: Cornelius, your prayers and alms are remembered by God
questions.explanation: Acts 10:4 says the angel told Cornelius that his prayers and alms are come up for a memorial before God.

questions.question: To whom was Cornelius instructed to send for help?
questions.correctAnswer: Simon Peter
questions.explanation: Acts 10:5 directs Cornelius to send men to Joppa to call for Simon, whose surname is Peter.

questions.question: Where was Simon Peter lodging when Cornelius sent for him?
options: At a tanner's house by the seaside
questions.correctAnswer: At a tanner's house by the seaside
questions.explanation: Acts 10:6 says Peter lodgeth with one Simon a tanner, whose house is by the seaside.

questions.question: Who did Cornelius call to send to Joppa after the angel departed?
options: Two household servants and a devout soldier
questions.correctAnswer: Two household servants and a devout soldier
questions.explanation: Acts 10:7 states Cornelius called two of his household servants and a devout soldier who waited on him continually.

questions.question: What time of day did Peter go up on the housetop to pray?
questions.correctAnswer: About the sixth hour
questions.explanation: Acts 10:9 tells that Peter went up upon the housetop to pray about the sixth hour.

questions.question: What happened to Peter while he was preparing to eat?
questions.correctAnswer: He fell into a trance
questions.explanation: Acts 10:10 explains that as they made ready, Peter fell into a trance.

questions.question: What did Peter see descending from heaven in his vision?
options: A great sheet knit at the four corners
questions.correctAnswer: A great sheet knit at the four corners
questions.explanation: Acts 10:11 describes a certain vessel descending unto Peter, like a great sheet knit at the four corners.

questions.question: True or False: Cornelius was a devout man who feared God and prayed to Him always.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Acts 10:2 states Cornelius was a devout man who feared God and prayed always.

questions.question: True or False: Peter was told in the vision to kill and eat whatever was shown to him.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Acts 10:13 quotes a voice telling Peter to rise, kill, and eat.

questions.question: True or False: The text says Peter immediately ate the unclean animals when told to do so.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Acts 10:14 records Peter saying he has never eaten anything common or unclean, showing he did not immediately eat.

questions.question: True or False: Cornelius was instructed to go to Jerusalem to meet Peter.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Acts 10:5 directs Cornelius to send men to Joppa for Peter, not to go to Jerusalem.

medium.title: Acts Chapter 10 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Acts Chapter 10 to real-life situations.

questions.question: What message did the Spirit give Peter about the men seeking him?
questions.correctAnswer: Three men seek thee
questions.explanation: The Spirit told Peter, 'Behold, three men seek thee' as stated in Acts 10:19.

questions.question: What does Acts 10:20 promise will happen if Peter 'arise therefore, and get thee down, and go with them, doubting nothing' as commanded in Acts 10:19?
options: The Spirit has sent them to him
He will be rejected by Cornelius
questions.correctAnswer: The Spirit has sent them to him
questions.explanation: Acts 10:20 says Peter should go with them without doubting because the Spirit has sent them.

questions.question: How did Peter respond when the men sent from Cornelius asked for him?
options: Behold, I am he whom ye seek
Tell Cornelius I will come later
questions.correctAnswer: Behold, I am he whom ye seek
questions.explanation: Peter openly declared to the men, 'Behold, I am he whom ye seek' as recorded in Acts 10:21.

questions.question: How does Acts 10:22 explain the reason Cornelius sent for Peter according to Acts 10:21?
options: Cornelius was warned by an holy angel to hear words from Peter
Cornelius sought to debate Peter on the law
Cornelius wanted Peter to heal him
questions.correctAnswer: Cornelius was warned by an holy angel to hear words from Peter
questions.explanation: Acts 10:22 states Cornelius was warned by an holy angel to send for Peter to hear his words.

questions.question: What does Peter say about calling any man common or unclean?
options: God hath shewed me that I should not call any man common or unclean
Only Jews are clean, others are common
The law forbids us to approach Gentiles
All others are unclean except the Jews
questions.correctAnswer: God hath shewed me that I should not call any man common or unclean
questions.explanation: Peter explains in Acts 10:28 that God showed him he should not call any man common or unclean.

questions.question: Why did Cornelius call for Peter according to Acts 10:29-32?
options: Because a man in bright clothing told him his prayers were heard
To have Peter perform a miracle
questions.correctAnswer: Because a man in bright clothing told him his prayers were heard
questions.explanation: Cornelius recounts a vision where a man in bright clothing told him his prayers were heard, prompting him to send for Peter as in Acts 10:30-32.

questions.question: What was Peter’s reaction when Cornelius fell down to worship him?
options: Stand up; I myself also am a man
questions.correctAnswer: Stand up; I myself also am a man
questions.explanation: Peter told Cornelius to stand up, saying he was also a man, according to Acts 10:26.

questions.question: How did Peter handle the cultural barrier between Jews and Gentiles as described in Acts 10:28?
options: He acknowledged it was unlawful but said God showed him not to call any man common or unclean
He refused to enter Cornelius's house
He preached only to the Jews present
He insisted Gentiles must follow Jewish customs
questions.correctAnswer: He acknowledged it was unlawful but said God showed him not to call any man common or unclean
questions.explanation: Peter recognized the law but explained God showed him to accept all men, as found in Acts 10:28.

questions.question: What practical lesson about obedience can be drawn from Peter's response to the Spirit's instruction in Acts 10:20-23?
options: Obedience without doubt leads to God’s guidance and fellowship
Delaying obedience is wise when unsure
questions.correctAnswer: Obedience without doubt leads to God’s guidance and fellowship
questions.explanation: Peter obeyed without doubting and went with the men, resulting in fellowship and the gospel being shared, as shown in Acts 10:20-23.

questions.question: What does the interaction between Peter and Cornelius teach about humility in Christian leadership?
options: Leaders should refuse worship and affirm their humanity
Leaders must always be treated as divine
Leaders should avoid all contact with non-believers
questions.correctAnswer: Leaders should refuse worship and affirm their humanity
questions.explanation: Peter refused Cornelius's worship and reminded him he was a man, demonstrating humility, as seen in Acts 10:25-26.

questions.question: How does Acts 10:24-25 illustrate the importance of community in receiving the gospel message?
options: Cornelius gathered his kinsmen and friends to hear Peter
questions.correctAnswer: Cornelius gathered his kinsmen and friends to hear Peter
questions.explanation: Cornelius assembled his relatives and near friends to hear Peter, emphasizing communal reception, Acts 10:24-25.

questions.question: What does the sending of men from Cornelius to Peter teach about prayer and action in faith?
options: Prayer leads to clear direction and prompt action
Prayer alone is sufficient without action
questions.correctAnswer: Prayer leads to clear direction and prompt action
questions.explanation: Cornelius’s prayer was answered through angelic instruction leading him to send men to Peter, as in Acts 10:3-8 and 10:30-32.

questions.question: How does Peter’s vision and subsequent obedience relate to God’s plan for inclusivity in Acts 10:9-16 and 10:17-23?
options: God is breaking barriers, calling Jews to accept Gentiles
God insists on strict separation of peoples
Peter ignores the vision and sticks to tradition
questions.correctAnswer: God is breaking barriers, calling Jews to accept Gentiles
questions.explanation: Peter’s vision prepared him to accept Gentiles, and he obeyed by going with Cornelius’s men, showing God’s inclusive plan, Acts 10:9-16, 10:17-23.

questions.question: True or False: Peter said it was lawful for a Jew to keep company with one of another nation before God showed him otherwise.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Peter acknowledged that it was unlawful for a Jew to keep company with one of another nation until God showed him otherwise, as in Acts 10:28.

questions.question: True or False: Cornelius fell at Peter’s feet and Peter accepted the worship gracefully.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Cornelius fell at Peter’s feet to worship him, but Peter told him to stand up and said he was a man, refusing the worship, Acts 10:25-26.

hard.title: Acts Chapter 10 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Acts Chapter 10.

questions.question: According to Acts 10:34, what truth did Peter openly proclaim?
options: God is no respecter of persons
The Messiah is yet to come
questions.correctAnswer: God is no respecter of persons
questions.explanation: Acts 10:34 states, 'Then Peter opened his mouth, and said, Of a truth I perceive that God is no respecter of persons:' showing Peter's realization that God's acceptance is not based on ethnicity.

questions.question: In Acts 10:36, how is Jesus Christ described in relation to all people?
options: He is a prophet only to Israel
He is King of the Jews
He is a teacher of righteousness
questions.correctAnswer: He is Lord of all
questions.explanation: Acts 10:36 says, 'The word which God sent unto the children of Israel, preaching peace by Jesus Christ: (he is Lord of all:)', indicating Jesus' universal lordship.

questions.question: What was the significance of Jesus being anointed with the Holy Ghost and power as described in Acts 10:38?
options: He went about doing good and healing all oppressed by the devil
He performed miracles only in Jerusalem
He preached only to the Gentiles
questions.correctAnswer: He went about doing good and healing all oppressed by the devil
questions.explanation: Acts 10:38 describes Jesus' ministry empowered by the Holy Ghost to do good and heal those oppressed by the devil, highlighting the divine empowerment of his mission.

questions.question: According to Acts 10:40, what event is described occurring on the third day?
questions.correctAnswer: God raised up Jesus
questions.explanation: Acts 10:40 states, 'Him God raised up the third day, and shewed him openly,' referencing the resurrection of Jesus on the third day.

questions.question: Who were the witnesses to Jesus' resurrection as mentioned in Acts 10:41?
options: Those chosen before of God who ate and drank with Him after He rose
questions.correctAnswer: Those chosen before of God who ate and drank with Him after He rose
questions.explanation: Acts 10:41 says Jesus was shown 'not to all the people, but unto witnesses chosen before of God, even to us, who did eat and drink with him after he rose from the dead,' emphasizing the select eyewitnesses.

questions.question: What command did Jesus give, as recorded in Acts 10:42?
options: To preach to the people and testify that He is ordained to be the Judge of quick and dead
To build a temple in Jerusalem
To perform miracles in His name
questions.correctAnswer: To preach to the people and testify that He is ordained to be the Judge of quick and dead
questions.explanation: Acts 10:42 records Jesus' command, 'And he commanded us to preach unto the people, and to testify that it is he which was ordained of God to be the Judge of quick and dead,' outlining the mission of the apostles.

questions.question: What does the Greek word 'dikaiosyne' in Acts 10:35 mean?
questions.correctAnswer: Righteousness
questions.explanation: 'Dikaiosyne' (δικαιοσύνη) in Acts 10:35 means 'righteousness,' referring to right conduct or justice before God, as seen in the phrase 'he that feareth him, and worketh righteousness, is accepted with him.'

questions.question: Which literary device is most evident in Peter's speech in Acts 10:34-43?
questions.correctAnswer: Inclusio
questions.explanation: Peter's speech in Acts 10:34-43 uses inclusio, framing the message with the theme of God accepting all peoples (verses 34 and 43), creating a literary bracket emphasizing universal salvation.

questions.question: Which Old Testament passage is echoed in Peter's declaration in Acts 10:34 that 'God is no respecter of persons'?
questions.correctAnswer: Deuteronomy 10:17
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 10:17 says 'The LORD your God is God of gods and Lord of lords, the great God, mighty and awesome, who shows no partiality and accepts no bribes,' directly correlating with Peter's statement in Acts 10:34.

questions.question: Which New Testament passage fulfills the theme of Gentiles receiving the Holy Ghost as found in Acts 10:44-46?
questions.correctAnswer: Romans 15:9-12
questions.explanation: Romans 15:9-12 speaks of Gentiles glorifying God for His mercy, fulfilling the theme in Acts 10:44-46 where the Holy Ghost falls on Gentiles, affirming God's acceptance of all nations.

questions.question: What event immediately precedes Peter's declaration in Acts 10:34 that God is no respecter of persons?
options: Cornelius and his household gathered to hear Peter
Peter receiving a vision about unclean animals
The Holy Ghost falling on the Gentiles
questions.correctAnswer: Cornelius and his household gathered to hear Peter
questions.explanation: Acts 10:33 immediately precedes verse 34 and describes Cornelius saying, 'Now therefore are we all here present before God, to hear all things that are commanded thee of God,' setting the context for Peter's speech.

questions.question: What is the cultural significance of Peter lodging with Simon the tanner as mentioned earlier in Acts 10:6, which frames the message in Acts 10:28?
options: Tanners were considered unclean, symbolizing acceptance of Gentiles
Tanners were high priests, symbolizing holiness
Tanners were Roman officials, symbolizing authority
Tanners were Jewish kings, symbolizing power
questions.correctAnswer: Tanners were considered unclean, symbolizing acceptance of Gentiles
questions.explanation: In Jewish culture, tanners handled dead animals and were considered ceremonially unclean; Peter lodging with a tanner (Acts 10:6) foreshadows his acceptance of Gentiles and breaking Jewish purity laws as explained in Acts 10:28.

questions.question: How does Peter’s vision of the sheet with unclean animals in Acts 10:11-16 function as a literary foreshadowing device?
options: It foreshadows the inclusion of Gentiles into the church
It predicts a famine in Judea
It symbolizes the destruction of Jerusalem
It foreshadows the coming of the Messiah
questions.correctAnswer: It foreshadows the inclusion of Gentiles into the church
questions.explanation: The vision of unclean animals being declared clean in Acts 10:11-16 foreshadows the breaking of dietary and ethnic barriers, indicating Gentiles' inclusion in the church.

questions.question: In Acts 10:43, the prophets give witness that through whose name remission of sins is granted?
questions.correctAnswer: Jesus
questions.explanation: Acts 10:43 states, 'To him give all the prophets witness, that through his name whosoever believeth in him shall receive remission of sins,' clearly identifying Jesus as the one through whom forgiveness is granted.

questions.question: True or False: In Acts 10:45, the Jewish believers were astonished because the Gentiles spoke in tongues and received the Holy Ghost.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Acts 10:45 states, 'they of the circumcision which believed were astonished...because that on the Gentiles also was poured out the gift of the Holy Ghost,' confirming their amazement at the Gentiles receiving the Spirit.

theological.title: Acts Chapter 10 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Acts Chapter 10 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What doctrine does Acts 10:34 teach about God's nature?
options: God is no respecter of persons
questions.correctAnswer: God is no respecter of persons
questions.explanation: Acts 10:34 explicitly states, 'Of a truth I perceive that God is no respecter of persons,' teaching that God does not show partiality based on ethnicity or social status.

questions.question: What doctrine about salvation does Acts 10:43 teach?
options: Remission of sins is received through faith in Jesus' name
Salvation is by works and adherence to the law
Faith must be accompanied by circumcision
questions.correctAnswer: Remission of sins is received through faith in Jesus' name
questions.explanation: Acts 10:43 states, 'through his name whosoever believeth in him shall receive remission of sins,' affirming salvation by faith in Jesus Christ alone.

questions.question: What doctrine about the Holy Spirit is taught in Acts 10:44?
options: The Holy Spirit falls on all who hear the word
The Holy Spirit is only given to Jewish believers
The Holy Spirit is received only after water baptism
The Holy Spirit chooses to indwell only apostles
questions.correctAnswer: The Holy Spirit falls on all who hear the word
questions.explanation: Acts 10:44 describes that 'the Holy Ghost fell on all them which heard the word,' indicating that the Spirit's reception is linked to hearing and believing the gospel, not ethnic background.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does Acts 10:31 specifically demonstrate?
questions.correctAnswer: Omniscience
questions.explanation: In Acts 10:31, God reveals to Cornelius that his prayers and alms are remembered, demonstrating God's omniscience in knowing the prayers and deeds of individuals.

questions.question: Which divine attribute is evidenced in Acts 10:20 when the Spirit commands Peter to go with the men without doubting?
questions.correctAnswer: Sovereignty
questions.explanation: Acts 10:20 shows God's sovereign guidance through the Spirit commanding Peter to go without doubt, illustrating God's control over the unfolding events.

questions.question: How does the vision in Acts 10:9-16 prepare the church for the inclusion of Gentiles?
options: It reveals that God declares all foods clean, symbolizing the removal of barriers between Jews and Gentiles
It mandates strict dietary laws to maintain Jewish purity
It commands only Jewish believers to evangelize Gentiles
It emphasizes that Gentiles must first convert to Judaism
questions.correctAnswer: It reveals that God declares all foods clean, symbolizing the removal of barriers between Jews and Gentiles
questions.explanation: The vision in Acts 10:9-16 where God declares previously unclean animals clean symbolizes the breaking down of Jewish ceremonial laws that separated them from Gentiles, preparing the church for Gentile inclusion.

questions.question: In what way does Acts 10:36-38 connect to the broader redemptive theme of Jesus as the Messiah?
options: It affirms Jesus’ anointing by the Holy Spirit to do good and heal, fulfilling messianic prophecy
It limits Jesus’ ministry only to Jews
It denies Jesus’ resurrection and divine power
It teaches Jesus was a political revolutionary
questions.correctAnswer: It affirms Jesus’ anointing by the Holy Spirit to do good and heal, fulfilling messianic prophecy
questions.explanation: Acts 10:36-38 describes Jesus’ anointing by the Holy Spirit and power to do good and heal, confirming His messianic role anticipated in Old Testament prophecy.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Acts 10:34 and Acts 10:35 teach about God's impartiality and acceptance?
options: God accepts anyone from any nation who fears Him and does righteousness
God accepts only Jews who keep the law perfectly
God's acceptance depends on social status
God shows favoritism based on ethnicity
questions.correctAnswer: God accepts anyone from any nation who fears Him and does righteousness
questions.explanation: Acts 10:34-35 affirm that God shows no partiality and accepts everyone who fears Him and works righteousness, regardless of national or ethnic background.

questions.question: What doctrine about the role of prophecy and witness is taught by combining Acts 10:39 and Acts 10:41?
options: The apostles are eyewitnesses chosen by God to testify of Jesus’ resurrection and works
Jesus’ resurrection is a myth without witnesses
Only Old Testament prophets are authoritative witnesses
questions.correctAnswer: The apostles are eyewitnesses chosen by God to testify of Jesus’ resurrection and works
questions.explanation: Acts 10:39 and 10:41 emphasize that the apostles were divinely chosen eyewitnesses who saw Jesus’ works, crucifixion, and resurrection, establishing the foundation for apostolic testimony.

questions.question: What theological synthesis about baptism and the Holy Spirit is taught by Acts 10:44-48?
options: Receiving the Holy Spirit precedes water baptism, and baptism follows as a public declaration
Water baptism is necessary to receive the Holy Spirit
The Holy Spirit is given only after baptism and confirmation
Baptism replaces the need for the Holy Spirit
questions.correctAnswer: Receiving the Holy Spirit precedes water baptism, and baptism follows as a public declaration
questions.explanation: Acts 10:44-48 shows the Gentiles receiving the Holy Spirit before water baptism, which Peter then commands, indicating that Spirit reception precedes baptism as a sign.

questions.question: Skeptics claim Acts 10:44-46 teaches that Gentiles must speak in tongues to receive the Holy Spirit. What does the passage actually teach?
options: The Holy Spirit was poured out on Gentiles, and speaking in tongues was a sign confirming this gift
Speaking in tongues is required for salvation
Only Jewish believers can receive the Holy Spirit
The passage forbids Gentiles from receiving the Spirit
questions.correctAnswer: The Holy Spirit was poured out on Gentiles, and speaking in tongues was a sign confirming this gift
questions.explanation: Acts 10:44-46 recounts the Gentiles receiving the Holy Spirit evidenced by speaking in tongues, showing the Spirit’s acceptance of Gentiles, not a requirement for salvation but a sign.

questions.question: What doctrine about prayer and almsgiving is taught by Acts 10:2?
options: Devout prayer and generous almsgiving are pleasing to God and remembered by Him
Prayer should be silent and private only
questions.correctAnswer: Devout prayer and generous almsgiving are pleasing to God and remembered by Him
questions.explanation: Acts 10:2 describes Cornelius as a man who prayed continually and gave generously, showing that such devotion is honored by God.

questions.question: Which divine attribute is demonstrated in Acts 10:4 when God acknowledges Cornelius’ prayers and alms as a memorial?
questions.correctAnswer: Omniscience
questions.explanation: Acts 10:4 reveals God's awareness and remembrance of Cornelius’ prayers and alms, demonstrating God's omniscience regarding human devotion.

questions.question: How does the sending of Peter to Cornelius in Acts 10:6 relate to the expansion of the gospel to the Gentiles?
options: It marks the divine initiative to break ethnic barriers and extend salvation beyond Israel
It emphasizes that only Jews are worthy of the gospel
It teaches that Gentiles must convert to Judaism first
It restricts the gospel to Jewish synagogues
questions.correctAnswer: It marks the divine initiative to break ethnic barriers and extend salvation beyond Israel
questions.explanation: Acts 10:6 shows God directing Cornelius to send for Peter, signaling the intentional outreach of the gospel to Gentiles, breaking Jewish exclusivism.

questions.question: What theological synthesis about divine guidance and human obedience is taught by Acts 10:19 and 10:20?
options: The Spirit instructs Peter to go with the men without hesitation, showing divine guidance requires human obedience
Divine guidance is optional for believers
The Spirit commands but does not expect obedience
questions.correctAnswer: The Spirit instructs Peter to go with the men without hesitation, showing divine guidance requires human obedience
questions.explanation: Acts 10:19-20 shows the Spirit explicitly telling Peter to go with the men without doubt, illustrating the necessity of obedient response to divine direction.
